author: kalo9480
content:
Hey guys! I've been looking into different CLs' implementation of direct calls to builders and found some interesting differences for the `X-Timeout-Ms` header.
```
┌────────────┬──────────────┬──────────────┐
│   Client   │ X-Timeout-Ms │ Configurable │
├────────────┼──────────────┼──────────────┤
│ Lighthouse │ 400          │ No           │
├────────────┼──────────────┼──────────────┤
│ Lodestar   │ 500          │ No           │
├────────────┼──────────────┼──────────────┤
│ Prysm      │ 600          │ Yes          │
├────────────┼──────────────┼──────────────┤
│ Teku       │ 1000         │ No           │
├────────────┼──────────────┼──────────────┤
│ Nimbus     │ 1500         │ No           │
├────────────┼──────────────┼──────────────┤
│ Grandine   │ 1000         │ No           │
└────────────┴──────────────┴──────────────┘
```

I'm not sure if this was discussed before, but has someone thought about having the same value here? I believe those differences will inevitably cause clients like Teku, Nimbus and Grandine to be building higher yielding blocks than let's say Lighthouse for the same builders. Not saying this is a good or bad thing, just something to note, as it may be a big driving factor for operators to switch to Teku/Nimbus/Grandine/configured Prysm. I know there are a lot of strong opinions regarding timing games here 🙂

author: kalo9480
content: IMO builders are expected to have fairly even geo distribution as they are directly incentivised the requests from proposers to have as low latency as possible. If this geo distribution is true or not, I do not have the data as of now. Also good to note that they should be using both `X-Timeout-Ms` and `Date-Milliseconds` in order to determine when to send the response back.

author: serenita_io
content:
One of the reasons why I really want to see this https://ptb.discord.com/channels/595666850260713488/1556640385789591564 

If a node operator runs 5 different client combinations, they shouldn't need to figure out these subtle differences between them, and configure each of them.

Timing games are going to be played, whether we make this timeout value configurable or not will not matter to "sophisticated" proposers.

My take:
- ship a sensible default, unified across all clients (I'm personally fine with up to 1000ms, as today, since Gloas blocks are much smaller)
- make it configurable
